frontend.prompt:
Implement the client-side behavior for GET /api/v1/items/ to match the contract. Include and respect the following facts exactly as written: [FACT:request-skip-type] [FACT:request-skip-minimum] [FACT:request-skip-default] [FACT:request-limit-type] [FACT:request-limit-minimum] [FACT:request-limit-maximum] [FACT:request-limit-default] [FACT:request-invalid-status] [FACT:response-count-scope] [FACT:response-empty-page-data]

Requirements for the frontend implementation:
- Query parameters: always send skip and limit as integers in the query string when fetching pages (e.g., ?skip=0&limit=20). The UI pagination controls must compute and send skip and limit directly (no page-number-only protocol).
- Defaults: if the user has not chosen paging values, use the contract defaults: skip = [FACT:request-skip-default], limit = [FACT:request-limit-default].
- Client-side validation: enforce that skip is an integer >= [FACT:request-skip-minimum] and limit is an integer between [FACT:request-limit-minimum] and [FACT:request-limit-maximum]. Prevent sending requests with invalid values; coerce or block inputs so only valid integers are sent.
- Handling server validation: if the server responds with status [FACT:request-invalid-status], treat it as parameter-validation failure: show a clear error to the user and avoid retrying with the same values without user correction.
- Response handling: display the returned data array as the current page. Use the returned count to show total items / enable/disable next/prev controls. The count represents items within the user's authorization and after server-side filtering (i.e., [FACT:response-count-scope]) and does not change based on the current page size. If the response contains an empty data array, treat it as empty page (i.e., display no items) per [FACT:response-empty-page-data].
- UX notes: when navigating pages compute new skip as previous_skip +/− limit. Disable Next when skip + returned data.length >= returned count. Keep all numeric values as integers when constructing queries.

backend.prompt:
Implement the server-side behavior for GET /api/v1/items/ to match the contract. Include and respect the following facts exactly as written: [FACT:request-skip-type] [FACT:request-skip-minimum] [FACT:request-skip-default] [FACT:request-limit-type] [FACT:request-limit-minimum] [FACT:request-limit-maximum] [FACT:request-limit-default] [FACT:request-invalid-status] [FACT:response-count-scope] [FACT:response-empty-page-data]

Requirements for the backend implementation:
- Parameter parsing and defaults: parse skip and limit from the query string and treat them as integers ([FACT:request-skip-type], [FACT:request-limit-type]). If skip is absent, default to [FACT:request-skip-default]. If limit is absent, default to [FACT:request-limit-default].
- Validation: reject requests where skip is not an integer or skip < [FACT:request-skip-minimum], or where limit is not an integer or limit < [FACT:request-limit-minimum] or limit > [FACT:request-limit-maximum]. For invalid parameters return the configured error status [FACT:request-invalid-status].
- Authorization & filtering: apply authorization and filtering first to determine the full matching set of items for the caller. Compute count over that set before applying pagination and return it as the response count; this must reflect the authorized+filtered total (i.e., [FACT:response-count-scope]).
- Pagination: after computing count, apply pagination using skip and limit to select the page of items to return in data. If the selected page is empty, return data exactly as an empty array per [FACT:response-empty-page-data].
- Response shape: return a JSON object containing at minimum 'data' (array of items for the requested page) and 'count' (the authorized+filtered total before pagination). Ensure numeric types are integers in the response where applicable.
- Error handling: for parameter validation failures use status [FACT:request-invalid-status] and include an explanatory payload identifying which parameter failed validation. Do not change or infer alternate paging semantics—enforce the exact bounds and defaults above.
